fields.name: num
fields.coerce: none: used as an array key (`player.items[num]`), so a number or a numeric string; any other value is an empty slot
fields.description: The slot of the stone: `stoneofxp`, `stoneofgold` or `stoneofluck`.

responses.name: Shells
responses.when: The stone is converted. The amount is 3,600 shells; for a stone that has `expires` (an activated one), it is `round(600 - 100 * days since expires)`. **Server bug:** that amount has no floor, so an old activated stone gives a negative amount, which `add_shells` takes from `cash` (the account save then fails its `cash < amount` check). Not on a `hardcore` or `test` server: there `add_shells` gives nothing and sends nothing, but the stone is still removed.

fields.name: phrase_args
fields.description: `{amount}`: the shells, as a formatted string (`to_pretty_num`).

fields.name: color
fields.description: The color of the log line.

responses.name: Updated
responses.when: After the shells: the slot is empty. A second `player` with `reopen: true` follows when the account update is saved.
responses.summary: Your state with `reopen: true`, `items[num]` set to `null` and the new `cash`.

confirm.note: The second `player` comes after the async account save at node/server.js:4810-4812

failures.intro: The handler sends no failure reply.

rows.when: No character. **Server bug:** the handler does not check for one. It throws on `player.items`.

replies.note: from the socket wrapper, with 16 more call cost

rows.when: The slot is empty, or it does not hold one of the three stones.

also.summary: The text `"+3,600"` (the amount) above you, in the shell color, with the `cash` sound.

order: later, a second `player` with `reopen: true` when the account update is saved
